newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine oil firms to re-test Calauit oil well.
newsitem.headline: Philippine oil firms to re-test Calauit oil well.

text.p: A ten-member consortium, led by Philippine National Oil Co-Exploration Corp, had started re-testing the Calauit oil field, the energy department said on Friday.

The department in a bulletin said the drilling, which began on Thursday, had yielded a flow rate of up to 6,578 barrels of oil per day. The group is conducting production tests to determine the commercial viability of the field.
"The operator is currently undertaking production logging to gather additional reservoir information prior to acidising the well to achieve a higher flow rate," the bulletin said.
The Calauit well was drilled and abandoned by its former operator in 1991.

The group has earmarked $5.5 million for the 50-day test period. If the results prove encouraging, the test period will extended by three to six months with an additional cost of $8.1 to $16.2 million, the bulletin added.
The field contains estimated reserves of two million to 80 million barrels of oil.

Other members of the consortium include Australia's SOCDET Production Pty ltd, Dragon (Far East) Ltd., Oriental Petroleum and Minerals Corp, Balabac Oil Exploration & Drilling Co, Basic Petroleum and Minerals, Unioil and Gas Development Co Inc, Palawan Oil and Gas Exploration Corp, TransAsia Oil and Energy Development Corp, and Sinophil Corp.
